title: Context-aware traffic orchestration and compatibility validation for progressive model rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a context-aware traffic orchestration layer to support canary rollouts, A/B tests, shadow traffic, and automatic rollback across region and capacity tiers. This ticket covers: routing policy primitives, semantic compatibility checks between model variants, session-sticky failover semantics, tiered capacity fallbacks, and the automated criteria that trigger rollbacks and routing shifts. The goal is to enable safer progressive deployments without manual intervention while preserving latency SLOs and minimizing customer-visible regressions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New routing policy API supports per-deployment rules: weight, region preference, capacity tier, and input classification tags. 2) Compatibility validator runs during deployment and blocks variant if tokenization mismatch, incompatible special tokens, or incompatible output schema is detected. 3) Canary traffic can be shadowed to a variant with configurable sample rate and independent observability. 4) Sticky-session routing persists variant choice for conversation sessions up to configurable TTL and falls back gracefully on variant mismatch or capacity loss. 5) Auto-rollback triggers on combined signal: latency degradation (p95 increase >30%), error rate spike (>1% absolute increase), or quality regression measured by embedding drift on canonical eval >0.12. 6) Documentation and runbook for on-call and release engineers included.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (experiment): implement routing primitives and compatibility validator in sandbox; route 1% shadow traffic to new variant for 2 weeks. Phase 2 (canary): enable 5% live canary in region-us-east and monitor SLOs and eval metrics for 72 hours. Phase 3 (ramped): progressively increase to 25% with sticky sessions and KV-cache warmup before session affinity. Phase 4 (global): enable region-aware weights and tiered fallback policies with automatic failover. Each phase gated by automated checks; manual hold allowed.
monitoring_and_alerting: - Per-variant metrics: request count, p50/p95 latency, token throughput, error rate, upstream 5xx, model-specific OOMs. - Quality signals: eval set pass rate, embedding cosine distance distribution vs baseline, hallucination proxy (low semantic overlap filter). - Health alarms: circuit-breaker trip, capacity tier saturated (>85%), tokenization errors. - Auto-rollback: alert and open rollback PR when threshold crossed; automated rollback executed after 3 consecutive 5-minute windows unless manually overridden.
compatibility_checks: - Tokenizer parity test using canonical dataset; mismatch blocks rollout. - Special-token and BOS/EOS policy check to ensure decoder compatibility. - Output schema conformance test using structured output harness (JSON-schema). - KV-cache binary compatibility test for warm-start between variant versions. - Model fingerprinting: architecture + vocab hash + quantization profile used to populate compatibility matrix.
fallback_strategy: - Tiered fallback: prefer same-variant in another region, then compatible lower-capacity variant, then safe conservative baseline model (e.g., smaller vocab-consistent model). - Session-sticky fallback: sessions stick to variant until variant becomes unavailable, then attempt to rehydrate session state via KV-cache best-effort and route to compatible variant with notification header. - Admission control: when budgeted dedicated capacity is exhausted, non-critical traffic is demoted to lower-tier models or queued based on customer policy.
migration_steps: 1) Build compatibility matrix generator job (daily). 2) Implement routing policy engine hooks in gateway and runtime (feature-flagged). 3) Add shadowing plumbing to observability pipeline and trace spans. 4) Add rollback controller that evaluates aggregated signals and performs canary weight decrement/rollbacks. 5) Run internal dogfood on low-risk models and iterate on thresholds. 6) Publish docs, runbook, and run a rehearsal incident to test failure modes.
notes: - Decision: use sequential probability ratio test (SPRT) for early detection of quality regressions combined with moving-window SLO checks for latency. - Trade-off: strict compatibility checks may block fast iteration; we will make some checks opt-outtable behind a release flag with audit logging. - KV-cache warmup before sticky routing reduces tail latency for canaries but requires additional cost; implement adaptive warmup only for sessions above token threshold.
